questions.question: Compare how far your chosen films reflect the auteur signature features of their filmmakers. (sample paper)
traps: Compare = weave both films into every paragraph (“whereas”, “similarly”), not film 1 then film 2.
If only one film is discussed, the mark scheme halves the band mark.
“How far / How useful” needs a judgement, argued in every paragraph and stated in the conclusion.

markScheme.rule: Levels-based: five bands, AO1 (knowledge, 20) and AO2 (application, 20) weighted equally. Pick the band that best fits the whole answer.
markScheme.focus: Auteur signatures (stylistic and thematic) in both films, and how far each film reflects them; the tension between a single auteur and collaboration.
indicative: Curtiz’s stylistic signature: crane and tracking shots, expressive shadows, dense foregrounds (Rick’s entrance, the market crane)
Curtiz’s weak thematic signature: a versatile studio workhorse; Schatz’s “genius of the system” (Wallis, the Epsteins, Steiner, Edeson, Bogart)
Penn’s thematic signature: sympathetic outsiders destroyed by a violent society (The Left Handed Gun, Little Big Man)
Collaborators on Bonnie and Clyde: Beatty as producer-star, Dede Allen’s editing, Benton and Newman’s New Wave script
Judgement on degree: Bonnie and Clyde reflects a stronger personal signature than Casablanca because New Hollywood gave directors more control
Band 5: constraints on the auteur (studio, Production Code, star persona vs director)

questions.modelAnswer:
Thesis: Bonnie and Clyde reflects its director’s signature far more than Casablanca, because Penn worked as the studio system collapsed while Curtiz worked inside it.

P1 Style: Curtiz’s crane into the market and the delayed reveal of Rick show a fluid-camera signature, whereas Penn’s signature lies in performance and sudden violence (the clerk shot through the glass).

P2 Themes: Penn returns to outsiders destroyed by society; Curtiz moved across genres, so Casablanca’s commitment theme comes from Wallis, the writers and wartime policy as much as from him.

P3 Collaboration: Casablanca as Schatz’s “genius of the system”; Bonnie and Clyde shaped by Beatty and Dede Allen, so even New Hollywood auteurism was collaborative.

Conclusion: to a large extent for Penn, to a limited extent for Curtiz; the auteur approach is more useful for New Hollywood than for the studio era.

questions.question: Compare how far your chosen films reflect their different production contexts. (sample paper)
traps: Compare = weave both films into every paragraph (“whereas”, “similarly”), not film 1 then film 2.
If only one film is discussed, the mark scheme halves the band mark.
“How far / How useful” needs a judgement, argued in every paragraph and stated in the conclusion.

markScheme.rule: Levels-based: five bands, AO1 (knowledge, 20) and AO2 (application, 20) weighted equally. Pick the band that best fits the whole answer.
markScheme.focus: How the studio system (1942) and its collapse (1967) shaped each film’s style, content and meaning.
indicative: Warner Bros. vertical integration: contract stars, director, composer; studio sets and fog at the airport
Production Code shaping Casablanca’s narrative resolution (Ilsa cannot leave her husband) and the searchlight dissolve
1948 Paramount ruling, TV, and Beatty as independent producer; Warner–Seven Arts as reluctant distributor
Collapse of the Code: graphic violence and sexuality in Bonnie and Clyde; ratings in 1968
Location shooting and New Wave influence vs studio-built exoticism
Judgement: both films are products of their institution, but Bonnie and Clyde ALSO helped change its context

questions.modelAnswer:
Thesis: both films reflect their production contexts to a significant extent, but Casablanca is shaped BY its institution, while Bonnie and Clyde helps reshape its own.

P1 Studio system vs independent producing (Wallis assigning the team vs Beatty buying the script).

P2 Censorship: the dissolve to the searchlight vs the clerk’s bloodied face.

P3 Technology and place: studio fog and Edeson’s chiaroscuro vs Guffey’s location light and slow-motion multi-camera ending.

Conclusion: to a large extent for both; the endings are the clearest proof.

questions.question: Compare how far your chosen films reflect the social and political contexts in which they were made.
traps: Compare = weave both films into every paragraph (“whereas”, “similarly”), not film 1 then film 2.
If only one film is discussed, the mark scheme halves the band mark.
“How far / How useful” needs a judgement, argued in every paragraph and stated in the conclusion.

markScheme.rule: Levels-based: five bands, AO1 (knowledge, 20) and AO2 (application, 20) weighted equally. Pick the band that best fits the whole answer.
markScheme.focus: The Second World War and intervention (1942) vs the 1960s counterculture, Vietnam and distrust of authority (1967).
indicative: Rick’s isolationism to commitment mirrors America entering the war; the anthem duel
Refugees, Vichy France, the Vichy water bottle
Bonnie and Clyde: a Depression setting read through 1960s youth rebellion and anti-establishment feeling
Televised Vietnam violence and the realistic, slow-motion ending
Contemporary setting (Casablanca) vs period setting (Bonnie and Clyde): the double layer of context
Judgement on how far context explains meaning versus genre or authorship

questions.modelAnswer:
Thesis: both films reflect their contexts closely, but Casablanca speaks about its present directly while Bonnie and Clyde uses the past as an allegory for the present.

P1 War vs counterculture through the heroes’ final choices.

P2 The anthem duel vs the foreclosed farm.

P3 Violence: Strasser’s clean death vs the bullet-ridden ending.

Conclusion: to a large extent; context shapes each film’s idea of heroism.

questions.question: “Hollywood films are the product of collaboration, not of a single author.” Compare how far this is true of your chosen films.
traps: Compare = weave both films into every paragraph (“whereas”, “similarly”), not film 1 then film 2.
If only one film is discussed, the mark scheme halves the band mark.
“How far / How useful” needs a judgement, argued in every paragraph and stated in the conclusion.

markScheme.rule: Levels-based: five bands, AO1 (knowledge, 20) and AO2 (application, 20) weighted equally. Pick the band that best fits the whole answer.
markScheme.focus: Evaluate the auteur approach against collaborative authorship in both films.
indicative: Casablanca: Wallis, the Epsteins and Koch, Steiner, Edeson, Bogart’s persona; the script rewritten during shooting
Bonnie and Clyde: Beatty, Benton and Newman, Robert Towne, Dede Allen, Guffey, Van Runkle
Arguments for a single author: Curtiz’s visual style; Penn’s themes and work with actors
Sarris vs Kael: three circles vs “Circles and Squares”
Stars as authors (Dyer): Bogart and Beatty
Judgement on which film better fits the statement

questions.modelAnswer:
Thesis: the statement is largely true of both, and especially of Casablanca, though Penn’s themes give Bonnie and Clyde a stronger single voice.

P1 Casablanca’s team. P2 Bonnie and Clyde’s team (Allen, Beatty). P3 The case for the director in each. P4 Stars as co-authors.

Conclusion: collaboration is the rule; the auteur is at most an orchestrator.

indicative: Casablanca: closure, sacrifice, “beautiful friendship”, La Marseillaise, fog
Production Code requirement that adultery not be rewarded
Bonnie and Clyde: no closure, slow-motion massacre, cut to black, no music
War-effort collectivism vs 1960s individual rebellion and distrust of the state

Conclusion: the endings are the films’ arguments.

questions.question: How far do your chosen films demonstrate a constant shift between passive and active spectatorship? Refer in detail to at least one sequence from each film. (sample paper)
traps: “Refer in detail to at least one sequence from each film” is an instruction: missing it caps the mark.
If only one film is discussed, the mark scheme halves the band mark.
“How far / How useful” needs a judgement, argued in every paragraph and stated in the conclusion.
Write impersonally: “the spectator is positioned”, never “I felt”.

markScheme.rule: Levels-based: five bands, AO1 (knowledge, 20) and AO2 (application, 20) weighted equally. Pick the band that best fits the whole answer.
markScheme.focus: Passive identification and active questioning in both films, through specific sequences and techniques.
indicative: Definitions: passive (absorbed, aligned) vs active (questioning, resisting, bringing context)
Joker: subway murders (subjective camera, cello) → guilty identification; Sophie reveal → active doubt
Get Out: Sunken Place (subjective camera, muffled sound) → immersion; auction and police-car ending → active reading
Murray Smith: alignment vs allegiance; Hall’s readings; hooks’ oppositional gaze
Viewing conditions and different spectators (Black and white audiences; fans vs critics)
Judgement on “constant”: is the shift constant, or concentrated at key moments?

questions.modelAnswer:
Thesis: both films shift the spectator between passive and active positions to a significant extent, though Joker does so to unsettle sympathy and Get Out to sharpen suspicion.

P1 Joker’s subway sequence (low-key lighting, claustrophobic framing, cello): passive alignment, then active horror.

P2 The Sophie reveal: editing replays scenes without her, forcing active re-reading.

P3 Get Out’s Sunken Place: restricted POV, falling motion, muffled sound = passive immersion; the teacup motif rewards active viewers.

P4 The police-car ending relies on spectators’ real-world knowledge: active spectatorship.

Conclusion: constant to a large extent; the shifts ARE each film’s meaning.

P1 Joker’s stair dance: palette, slow motion and music. P2 The cello after the subway. P3 Get Out’s teacup and Sunken Place. P4 The police lights at the end.

Conclusion: important to a significant extent, but not alone.

questions.question: How useful has an ideological critical approach been in understanding the narrative resolution of your chosen films? (sample paper)
traps: “How useful … ideological critical approach” = evaluate the APPROACH, not just describe the ideology.
If only one film is discussed, the mark scheme halves the band mark.
Every paragraph needs a named scene AND a named technique (your teacher’s target 1).

markScheme.rule: Levels-based: five bands, AO1 (knowledge, 20) and AO2 (application, 20) weighted equally. Pick the band that best fits the whole answer.
markScheme.focus: Apply ideology to each ending and evaluate how much it explains.
indicative: Trainspotting: Renton steals the money; “Choose Life” bookends; individualism over loyalty (Thatcherism)
Shaun: the news montage; zombies as labour; parodied Todorov equilibrium (Marxist)
Film form in the endings: “Born Slippy”, walking to camera; channel-flicking montage
What ideology reveals that a purely narrative reading misses
Limits: irony, comedy and genre pleasure; ambiguous endings
Judgement on usefulness

questions.modelAnswer:
Thesis: an ideological approach is highly useful for both resolutions, because each ending exposes how capitalism absorbs rebellion, though comedy and irony limit a single reading.

P1 Renton’s theft: voiceover returns inverted; Thatcherite individualism.

P2 Shaun’s montage: capitalism absorbs the undead; the new equilibrium = the old.

P3 Comparison: both endings are ironic “happy endings”.

P4 Limits: Renton’s gift to Spud; Shaun keeps Ed out of love, not ideology.

Conclusion: very useful, but not sufficient alone.

Ideology shows the oppositions collapsing: Renton swaps one addiction for another; Shaun is already a zombie

Judgement

questions.modelAnswer:
Thesis: ideology is very useful because in both films the oppositions are revealed as false.

P1 Heroin vs life. P2 Living vs undead (mirrored walks). P3 Masculine oppositions. P4 Limits.

Conclusion.
